title: Roof Removal with a Crane: Brace Free-Standing Walls and Use Radios
summary: A worker giving crane signals was killed when a 4-foot brick parapet wall collapsed as a roof section was lifted free. The wall was not braced and he stood below it. Brace tall walls and use two-way radios so signal people can stand in safe places.
talking_points: A crew removed a roof from a fire-damaged two-story building by cutting it into sections about 25 feet square and lifting each one with a 75-ton crane. The crane operator could not see the load, so a coworker gave hand signals from a second-story window.
As a roof section lifted off, the brick parapet wall above that window fell inward. Removing the roof had left a free-standing brick wall more than one story tall, with no lateral bracing.
Brace free-standing walls more than one story high with lateral bracing. The wall was not built to stand alone once the roof was removed.
Use two-way radios between the crane operator and the signal person. With a radio, the signal person can stand where the roof is already gone and falling material cannot reach.
Before a lift, ask where this wall, roof edge, or load will fall if it shifts. Keep people out of that area.
Pick the signal person's position for safety first, not only for line of sight.
site_hazards_to_check: Brick parapets or walls left free-standing after the roof or floors are removed
No lateral bracing on walls over one story
Signal person standing under or beside walls, edges, or loads
Crane operator with no line of sight and no radio
Fire-damaged or vacant buildings with weakened structures
discussion_questions: Which walls will be free-standing during this work, and how are they braced?
Where will the signal person stand, and what could fall on that spot?
How will the crane operator and signal person communicate?

flags: Verified 29 CFR 1926.854(b) (eCFR): a wall section more than one story high may not stand alone without lateral bracing, so the bracing point is supported. 1926.1419 (signals, general) and 1926.1420 (radio/electronic signals) are valid Subpart CC sections; the radio point is a MN FACE recommendation and the talk words it as one.
